definition: Digital applications for climate adaptation provide users with information, recommendations or decision support specifically intended to help them respond or adapt to climate risks. Counts when the project finances, develops, procures or deploys an application or digital service with an explicit adaptation function, such as climate-informed agricultural advice, drought-management support or adaptation decision tools. The application must support an adaptation decision or action; merely displaying climate information belongs to climate_information_systems, while issuing hazard warnings belongs to ews. Does not count for climate-smart practices with no digital component, generic digital services with no stated adaptation function, climate information provided only as context, or applications developed outside the project. The application must give a recommendation or advice for a specific action by its users (when to plant, how much to irrigate, which variety to choose, how to protect stock or property); a data platform, dashboard or portal that makes climate information available to inform decisions or policy is climate_information_systems. Does not count: a system that issues alerts or warnings (ews); surveillance, modelling, mapping, land information systems or master plans (climate_information_systems or climate_governance); supply-chain or logistics systems; preparedness simulations or drills; programmes that incubate startups which may build such tools.
boundary: The project gives users digital advice on a specific action to take against climate risk.
note: Keep distinct from climate_information_systems and ews.
